title: Risks of Racing: Russian and Chinese Perceptions of Strategic Competition in the Euro-Atlantic Region

As the United States and its allies invest more in their nuclear forces to deter Russia and China, some have warned of an impending arms race. The likelihood of an arms race, however, depends on perceptions in Moscow and Beijing. The CSIS Project on Nuclear Issues (PONI) drew from historical sources and expert workshops to evaluate how Russia and China would view and respond to four U.S. and UK buildup scenarios.The study found that Russia and China are unlikely to abandon their nuclear modernization and expansion programs due to domestic factors and long-standing distrust of the United States. Both countries, though, may view investments in certain capabilities as more escalatory than others. Accordingly, the United States and its allies should tailor deterrence and risk reduction efforts to Russian and Chinese threat perceptions.
